name: When do I need to build a kitchen addition instead of reconfiguring my layout?

mainEntity.name: When do I need to build a kitchen addition instead of reconfiguring my layout?

acceptedAnswer.text: You need a kitchen addition when your current kitchen cannot support your household needs and surrounding interior walls cannot be moved. Common reasons include needing space for a functional layout, adding an eat-in dining area, building a walk-in pantry, or accommodating multiple cooks. If an open-concept layout is impossible because removing adjacent interior walls would eliminate essential rooms like bedrooms or baths, extending outward is the best option. An addition lets you design the room from scratch rather than compromising within an undersized existing footprint.
acceptedAnswer.description: You need an addition when your current interior walls cannot be moved or expanded without sacrificing essential living spaces, but you still require extra square footage.
